The proposed controller is implemented on Sandia National Laboratories’ Secure Scalable Microgrid (SSM) Testbed [16]. The switching frequency for the hardware is 10 kHz. Controller and switching logic are implemented using a SpeedGoat. Also, for the hardware test the controller gains are as follow: K0 = 0.5; Kz = 0.5; k = 1.0; p p p K0 = 335; Kz = 335; k = 670. i i i The common mode voltage is stepped to produce a prolonged offset as shown in Fig. 29. The common mode offset steps by 60V. It can be seen from Fig. 30, that current very slightly deviates from the steady-state at the inception of the CM step, but recovers within about 1/4 of a cycle. This is much faster than the simulation results. This may be because the simulated voltage step was instantaneous which is not possible on hardware. Additionally, there may be additional damping (resistance) that was not accounted for in the model. Figure 29: Hardware Test: Grid-end voltage.
